title: Bootstrap Rust CLI
description: Create the installable Rust binary, package metadata, clap command surface, and prime/help command for the agent-orchestrator project. Keep the CLI usable without Herdr installed and report clear errors for unavailable integrations.

title: Read SQ dependency tree
description: Implement the SQ JSONL reader, task model, scope selection, dependency validation, and ready-task calculation. SQ is the contract; detect cycles, missing blockers, unrelated tasks, plan drift, and tasks already owned by another run.

title: Manage Herdr agent panes
description: Implement Herdr integration for creating named workspaces or panes, launching OMP agents with task context, retaining pane/session handles, observing process state, and reporting unavailable Herdr cleanly. Keep the integration behind a narrow driver boundary.

title: Correlate identities and handoffs
description: Integrate agent-id current/discover and AgentMail JSON sends. Generate complete handoffs containing orchestrator identity, task ID, queue path, worktree, branch, dependencies, acceptance criteria, and message receipts; reconcile agent reports with SQ transitions.

title: Provision worktrees and reconcile runs
description: Implement worktree and branch provisioning, canonical queue sharing, runtime ledger, leases, status reconciliation, blocked/failed/lost worker handling, and a finish loop that unlocks dependent SQ tasks without silently retrying or merging.

title: Test install and workflow
description: Add behavior-focused tests for graph readiness, scope, handoffs, unavailable integrations, and state transitions. Add the agent-facing prime manual and command help, document installation and local assumptions, and run the focused checks.

title: Converge independent blocker branches safely
description:
Problem: a task can depend on two or more independent completed blockers whose task branches diverged from a common base. The current planner can identify a unique blocker branch only when one branch already descends from every other blocker; otherwise it refuses with AmbiguousBlockerBranches. It does not merge, cherry-pick, or create a convergence branch, so a valid graph with independent prerequisites cannot be dispatched. Do not weaken this refusal by choosing one branch or trusting mutable branch tips.

Goal: design and implement an explicit, auditable convergence strategy for a ready task with multiple completed blocker commits. Preserve the current invariants: the canonical SQ queue remains authoritative; only the scoped graph is touched; blocker reports and deliverables are accepted before downstream provisioning; no silent retries; no accidental merges into the repository's main branch; and every resulting branch/worktree/ledger handle remains verifiable across restart.

Potential solutions to evaluate:
1. Orchestrator-created convergence branch: choose a deterministic accepted blocker commit as the base, create a dedicated convergence worktree/branch, merge each other accepted blocker commit, validate the merge, then base the dependent task on the convergence commit. Decide naming, ownership, ledger stages, Herdr workspace lifecycle, conflict handling, and whether a worker or orchestrator resolves conflicts.
2. Worker-owned integration task: require the SQ graph to represent convergence explicitly as a task that depends on all blockers. Dispatch that task with all accepted blocker commits in its handoff; the worker performs and validates the merge, reports one commit, and the downstream task uses that report. This keeps Git mutation in a worker but adds graph authoring overhead.
3. Deterministic cherry-pick/replay: apply accepted blocker commits onto one base in a dedicated branch. Evaluate commit identity, conflict behavior, multi-commit blockers, and whether replay violates provenance or creates surprising duplicate commits.
4. Require pre-integrated blocker branches: keep refusing divergent branches and document that users must integrate them manually before declaring the dependent task ready. Evaluate simplicity against the loss of automation and the current dogfood use case.

Acceptance criteria for the eventual implementation: multiple independent blockers either converge through an explicitly selected and recorded strategy or stop with a precise actionable error; no branch is silently discarded; conflicts are visible and terminal; the dependent task starts only from the validated convergence commit; restart/reconciliation is idempotent; branch and worktree cleanup semantics are explicit; and focused tests cover two independent blockers, already-linear blockers, conflicts, missing/invalid reports, reruns, and unrelated queue isolation.

metadata.priority_rationale: blocked valid dependency graphs need an explicit safe integration strategy
